title: In 1966, the Sky Over Arizona Rained 40 Meteors Every Second

scenes.text: In 1966, the sky over Arizona rained 40 meteors every second.
On November 17, astronomers on Kitt Peak counted a storm of falling stars.
One sweep suggested 144,000 meteors an hour.
The peak lasted about fifteen to twenty minutes. Watchers said the meteors fell like a giant umbrella.
It happens when Earth plows through a trail of dust left by a comet.
Forty falling stars a second. Not in a movie. In 1966.

description:
In 1966, observers on Kitt Peak in Arizona counted about 40 meteors every second during the Leonid storm.
The peak lasted about 15 to 20 minutes.
Have you ever seen a meteor shower?
first_comment: What is the most shooting stars you have ever seen at once?
